data.content:
The borrower of a digital loan has an explicit option to exit during a cooling-off period set by the NBFC's credit policy (minimum one day) by paying the principal and proportionate APR with no penalty, and the NBFC may retain a reasonable one-time processing fee if the borrower exits in that window, which must be disclosed upfront in the KFS (Credit Facilities Directions 2025, para 11).

Note that the passage does not explicitly say how the repayment is treated beyond principal and proportionate APR, and it does not state a refund mechanism for the processing fee. After the cooling-off period, prepayment continues to be allowed under the Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025, which I did not pull up.

content.text: The corpus does not say whether a single tap counts as explicit consent to loan terms, and it sets no record-keeping standard for loan acceptance. The closest rule is Para 13(1) of the NBFC Credit Facilities Directions 2025, which requires "prior and explicit consent of the borrower having audit trail" for collecting borrower data through digital lending apps, and Para 13(3), which requires the purpose of consent to be disclosed at each stage. Para 13 covers data consent, not acceptance of loan terms, so it does not settle the single-tap question. The Key Fact Statement provisions (Para 9 of the Credit Facilities Directions and Para 29 of the Responsible Business Conduct Directions) may bear on what the borrower must be shown before accepting, but I did not read them in full.

content.text: The corpus requires a copy of the loan agreement and its enclosures "at the time of sanction / disbursement" (RBI NBFC Responsible Business Conduct Directions 2025, paras 14 and 27), but it does not prescribe a delivery channel for that copy or a number of days after sanction. For digital loans, the Credit Facilities Directions 2025 (para 9(3)) require digitally signed documents, including the KFS, sanction letter and terms and conditions, to flow automatically to the borrower's registered and verified email or SMS on execution of the loan contract. Para 13 of the Responsible Business Conduct Directions also requires the sanction amount and terms, including the annualised rate of interest, to be conveyed in writing in a language the borrower understands. I did not retrieve the KFS-specific paragraph, so the KFS timing rules are not covered here.

content.text: Yes. Para 29(1) of the RBI NBFC Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 requires an NBFC to provide a Key Fact Statement to all prospective retail and MSME term borrowers "before executing the loan contract," and para 29(3) requires it to include the APR computation (APR covers all charges levied by the NBFC) and the loan's amortisation schedule. Showing these only after the borrower accepts would not meet that sequencing. The KFS's validity period (para 29(2)) also indicates the borrower must see the terms before agreeing to them. The corpus does not state the "after acceptance" point in those exact words, so that conclusion rests on the "before executing" wording.

findings.obligation: An NBFC must give every prospective retail borrower a KFS in the standard format before the loan contract is executed. The KFS must include the APR computation sheet and the amortisation schedule, be explained to the borrower, and carry an acknowledgement of understanding. It must also stay valid for at least three working days.
findings.recommendation: Show the full KFS, with APR, fees and repayment schedule, before the borrower can tap Accept. Give it a unique proposal number and a validity of at least three working days. Obtain an acknowledgement that the contents were explained and understood. Showing these terms only after acceptance is not permissible.

11. Cooling-off period
(1) The borrower shall be given an explicit option to exit a digital loan by paying
the principal and the proportionate APR without any penalty during an initial
“cooling-off period”. The cooling off period shall be determined by the NBFC in
terms of their credit policy, subject to the period so determined not being less
than one day. For borrower continuing with the loan even after cooling-off
period, pre-payment shall continue to be allowed as per Reserve Bank of India
(Non-Banking Financial Companies- Responsible Business Conduct)
Directions, 2025.
(2) An NBFC may retain a reasonable one-time processing fee, if the customer
exits the loan during the cooling-off period. This, if applicable, shall be
disclosed to the customer upfront in KFS.

9. Disclosures to borrowers
(1) An NBFC shall provide a Key Fact Statement (KFS), as per instructions
contained in Reserve Bank of India (Non- Banking Financial Companies –
Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025.
(2) As regards penal charges, an NBFC shall be guided by Reserve Bank of India
(Non- Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct)
Directions, 2025.
(3) An NBFC shall ensure that digitally signed documents (on the letter head of
the NBFC) viz., KFS, summary of loan product, sanction letter, terms and
conditions, account statements, privacy policies of the NBFC / LSP with
respect to storage and usage of borrowers’ data, etc. shall automatically flow
to the borrower on the registered and verified email / SMS upon execution of
the loan contract / transactions.
Note: Digitally signed documents shall be in compliance with the provisions of
the Information Technology Act, 2000, as amended from time to time.
(4) An NBFC shall maintain a website of its own in public domain, which shall be
kept up to date, inter-alia, with the following details at a prominent single place
on the website for ease of accessibility:
(i) Details of all of its digital lending products and its DLAs.
(ii) Details of LSPs and the DLAs of the LSPs along with the details of the
activities for which they have been engaged for.
(iii) Particulars of NBFC’s customer care and internal grievance redressal
mechanism.
(iv) Link to the Reserve Bank’s Complaint Management System (CMS) and
Sachet Portal.
(v) Privacy policies and other details as required under extant guidelines of the
Reserve Bank.
(5) An NBFC shall ensure that DLAs / LSPs have links to the above website of the
NBFC.

13. Collection, usage and sharing of data with third parties
(1) An NBFC shall ensure that any collection of data by their DLA and DLA of their
LSP is need-based and with prior and explicit consent of the borrower having
audit trail. In any case, an NBFC shall also ensure that DLA of NBFC / LSP
desist from accessing mobile phone resources like file and media, contact list,
call logs, telephony functions, etc. A one-time access can be taken for camera,
microphone, location or any other facility necessary for the purpose of on-
boarding / KYC requirements only, with the explicit consent of the borrower.
(2) The borrower shall be provided with an option to give or deny consent for use
of specific data, restrict disclosure to third parties, data retention, revoke
consent already granted to collect personal data and if required, make the
NBFC / LSP delete / forget the data.
(3) The purpose of obtaining borrowers’ consent needs to be disclosed at each

term loans sanctioned on or after October 1, 2024, including fresh loans to existing
customers, by an NBFC. Credit card receivables are exempted from the provisions
given below:
(1) An NBFC shall provide a KFS to all prospective borrowers to help them take an
informed view before executing the loan contract, as per the standardised format
given in the Annex I. The KFS shall be written in a language understood by such
borrowers. Contents of KFS shall be explained to the borrower and an
acknowledgement shall be obtained that they have understood the same.

validity period of at least three working days for loans having tenor of seven days
or more, and a validity period of one working day for loans having tenor of less than
seven days.

provided the KFS by the NBFC, to agree to the terms of the loan. The NBFC shall

during the validity period.
